sn51.22:1.2: It is typical of Ānanda to ask the Buddha on such matters. Here he elicits from the Buddha a fascinating and unique description of his meditative methods for developing special abilities.
sn51.22:1.5: I am not sure if it is possible to determine which method he used in specific instances. In several cases he is said to have disappeared from where he was and reappeared in the realm of divinity (eg. [sn6.5](), [mn49:3.2]()). It seems reasonable to deduce that this was his ordinary physical body, because he disappeared from his normal place. A mind-made body is a separate entity ([mn77:30.1]()), so the physical body should remain where it is. On the other hand, the same expression is used when he approached Anuruddha, who explicitly says it was a mind-made body ([an8.30:23.3]()).
sn51.22:4.1: On the physics of this see [dn23:17.5]().
